a systematic study of the effects of the design of high temperature (HT) permanent magnet machines on their performance, with the objective of reducing the torque ripples and power losses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the choice of magnetic wedges and magnet segmentation has a significant influence on the power losses in permanent magnet machines, but it is not a decisive factor in the overall thermal performance.
the design of the magnetic wedges is a key parameter for reducing the power losses, cogging torque and vibration in HT PM machines.
the choice of materials and design of permanent magnet machines has a strong impact on power losses, cogging torque and performance at high temperatures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the design of permanent magnet synchronous machines for HT applications requires a careful consideration of the material properties of magnets, wedges, and windings.
, in general, magnet segmentation and the use of non-ferromagnetic wedges in the stator of HT machines are beneficial in terms of reducing the power losses and the cogging torque.

the use of wedges made of soft magnetic materials, such as Fe-Si or Fe-Cu, can reduce the torque ripple and power losses in the magnets by up to 20% compared to wedges made from the magnets themselves.
The main takeaway from our work is that
magnet segmentation and use of wedges made of high conductivity material are the two key factors that reduce the power losses in the permanent magnets.
the choice of the material used in the wedges and the magnet segmentation are important factors in determining the performance of HT machines.
